goals: Mechanistic: quantify precipitation partitioning into surface runoff, ET, and recharge/drainage across the Naches HUC8 and attribute it to elevation-driven forcing and soil texture
Validation: compare simulated SWE to SNOTEL and simulated water table to USGS wells; assess water-balance closure

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves the full 1-D water balance (ET, runoff, drainage, snow, soil moisture) at each point; spatial sampling spans basin heterogeneity. CONUS location gives elevation-resolved NLDAS forcing, so the elevation gradient is partially represented.

answerable: Precipitation partitioning (ET, surface runoff, sub-surface drainage/recharge) per column, given WTD-informed warm start and multi-year NLDAS forcing
Elevation control on partitioning via NLDAS orographic precip/temperature and simulated snow (coarse, 12 km)
SWE validation against SNOTEL (H2OSNO/QSNOMELT in default output)
Water-table validation against co-located USGS wells (with expected 1-D vs lateral-equilibrium drift)

not_answerable.aspect: Validation of the runoff term against USGS stream gauges
not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral routing; columns are independent 1-D points with no integrated streamflow

not_answerable.aspect: Direct validation of the ET term
not_answerable.needs: flux-tower / eddy-covariance ingest or analog-site ET dataset

not_answerable.aspect: Sub-12 km elevation effect on snow at ridgetops
not_answerable.why: NLDAS 12 km cells average over terrain; no within-cell lapse rate, so high-station SWE is underestimated

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation band x dominant soil texture), with validation columns pinned to observation sites

classes: dominant SSURGO texture per band (expander-resolved, ~3 classes)

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 elevation bands x ~3 dominant soil textures = 12 skeleton cells spanning the drivers, plus 2 extra columns oversampling the rain-snow transition where snowmelt-driven recharge/runoff is most sensitive. Smallest set that resolves both axes without a blind grid.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate in the rain-snow transition band (1100-1500 m) where snowpack partitioning between melt-runoff and recharge is most variable; sample valley bottoms for the deepest-storage/recharge end-member and high band for snow-dominated regime. Within each band pick the dominant SSURGO texture(s).
sampling_strategy.replication: Light (2 replicate columns) only in the rain-snow transition band, which drives the largest partitioning uncertainty.

sampling_plan.reason: Deepest storage / recharge end-member; low-precip, snow-free regime for the drainage term.
Transitional ET-dominated regime spanning mid-elevation soil textures.
Most sensitive partitioning zone (melt-runoff vs recharge); oversampled and lightly replicated.
Snow-dominated regime controlling melt timing and high-elevation recharge.
Pinned to the 6 SNOTEL stations for co-located SWE validation.
Pinned to well locations for co-located WTD validation (count is data-density dependent).

validation_design.comparison: co-located — nearest column to each SNOTEL site; expect ridgetop underestimation from 12 km forcing
validation_design.metric: bias + RMSE on peak SWE and melt-out timing

validation_design.comparison: co-located — requires WTD-informed warm start; expect drift from 1-D vs lateral equilibrium
NOT comparable without routing — flagged as gap, not validated
no direct validation; only water-balance closure (P = ET + runoff + drainage + dStorage)

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing, native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start, multi-year run (spin-up years for slow states)

requires_capabilities.why: Recharge and water table are slow states; cold start gives ~0 recharge and meaningless ZWT
Slow states must equilibrate; NLDAS gives elevation-resolved precip driving the partitioning gradient
Single-column ELM produces no integrated streamflow

requires_capabilities.capability: Flux-tower / ET observation ingest (or analog dataset)
requires_capabilities.blocks: direct validation of the ET term

requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS averages over terrain within 12 km cells
requires_capabilities.blocks: accurate ridgetop SWE and fine elevation partitioning

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM elevation sampling + SSURGO soil sampling + HUC8 boundary resolver
requires_capabilities.why: Expander needs these to turn bands into concrete points

requires_capabilities.capability: SNOTEL and USGS well observation ingest
requires_capabilities.why: Needed to pin and score validation columns

assumptions: SSURGO yields ~3 resolvable dominant soil textures across the elevation bands (exact classes set by expander).
NLDAS-2 covers the full Naches bbox (CONUS) so all columns get elevation-resolved forcing.
USGS well records exist at enough locations for co-located WTD validation; count is data-dependent.
Baseline forcing period is a multi-year window within 1980-2018 including spin-up; exact years set downstream.
Water-balance closure (not observation) is the only check available for ET.
open_questions: How many USGS wells have usable WTD records inside the HUC8, and at what depths?
Which SNOTEL stations fall inside the bbox vs need nearest-column mapping?
Is a routing/aggregation step planned so the 93 stream gauges can eventually be used?
Preferred analysis period / climatology window for the partitioning quantification?
